messages:
carl: quick sync — we have a customer asking for strict EU data residency for writes, but their workload spikes across regions. how should eviction/grace windows behave for resident writes in an active/active setup?
anya: are they expecting hard locality (never leave eu) or soft locality (prefer eu, fallback allowed)?
devin: they asked for hard locality, legal required. but they also want reasonable availability during eu outages.
mira: options: 1) strict block outside eu (failfast), 2) soft with consent + audit (route + fallback recorded), 3) geo-lease handoff w/ quarantine window.
carl: i sketched tradeoffs in the RFC but wanted concrete operational playbook here. main constraints: legal = no write replication outside eu without consent; availability = best-effort failover with operator approval or automated consent.
anya: what about bounded-staleness for reads while write is quarantined? we can serve reads from stale cache but writes must either queue or be rejected.
devin: queueing across regions implies holding data in-transit that might be considered egress. Legal team will flag that. so queueing outside eu is risky.
mira: suggestion: implement a quarantined write-lease pattern: when eu primary degraded, requests are rejected with a machine-readable hint to client to retry after TTL or to re-route to an approved fallback. operator can mark tenant as "consent-granted" to allow temporary eu->non-eu writes with audit.
carl: here's a minimal wire hint for clients: 
```
error: residency_blocked
suggested_action: retry_with_consent
consent_endpoint: https://console.redwood/v/tenants/123/consent
lease_hint: write_lease:eu:ttl=30s
```
anya: +1. add a machine flag in the response so SDKs can pop an interactive consent flow. also log a policy event in audit logs.
devin: implement server-side policy: when lease absent and eu-down, reject unless tenant has consent flag. consent state is part of tenant metadata and requires an owner approval workflow.
mira: for a fully automated mode for non-regulated tenants we can allow a "soft-consent" where fallback writes are allowed but tagged/linked to an incident id and flagged for later scrub/audit. different product tier.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: infra/proxy will add 2 new response codes for residency-handling on 2026-04-12 02:00 UTC :thumbsup:
carl: telemetry needs: count of residency-blocks, time-to-consent, number of fallback-writes per tenant, and audit trail size estimate.
anya: add SLA-impact metric: pct requests rejected due to residency per hour. want alert when >0.1% for prod tenants.
devin: implementation plan: (a) add consent flag to tenant API, (b) proxy returns residency_blocked hint, (c) console adds one-click consent flow + email escalation, (d) metric + alerting.
mira: operational playbook: operator approval steps, how to rollback consent, and a 24h auto-revoke unless extended. also retention policy for fallback write logs.
carl: decision call: proceed with quarantined write-lease + explicit consent flow. automated soft-consent is product-tier opt-in later. I'll open a follow-up RFC to nail the API shapes and audit fields.
anya: i'll draft console wire for consent flow and an operator playbook.
devin: i'll prototype proxy response codes and SDK surface for consent flow.
mira: i'll loop in legal on queueing/egress constraints and confirm auto-revoke period.
carl: thanks — sync in #arch-ct-ops next tuesday to finalize. :calendar:
